title: N-Queens
prompt:
The n-queens puzzle asks you to place n chess queens on an n x n chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no two queens share a row, column, or diagonal). The classic version of this problem returns every distinct board layout; this variant returns the COUNT of valid arrangements rather than the board layouts themselves, which keeps the test harness simple while still exercising the full backtracking logic needed to solve n-queens.

Given an integer `n`, return the number of distinct solutions to the n-queens puzzle.

examples.explanation: There are exactly 2 distinct ways to place 4 non-attacking queens on a 4x4 board.
A single queen on a 1x1 board trivially doesn't attack anything.

hints: Since no two queens can share a row, you can place exactly one queen per row and recurse row by row, choosing which column to place it in.
Track which columns, and which diagonals, are already occupied. For an n x n board, a cell (row, col) lies on diagonal (row - col) and anti-diagonal (row + col) — use sets to mark these as taken.

Backtrack: at each row, try every column not already blocked by an occupied column or diagonal; place the queen (mark column/diagonal/anti-diagonal used), recurse to the next row, then unmark on backtrack. When you successfully place a queen in every row, increment your solution counter.

solution.approach: Place queens one row at a time via backtracking, since no valid solution can ever have two queens in the same row. Track three sets: occupied columns, occupied diagonals (identified by row - col, constant along a top-left-to-bottom-right diagonal), and occupied anti-diagonals (identified by row + col, constant along a top-right-to-bottom-left diagonal). At each row, try every column: if the column and both diagonals through this cell are free, place the queen (add to all three sets), recurse to the next row, then remove from all three sets to backtrack. When the recursion reaches row == n, a full valid placement has been found, so increment the solution count.
solution.code:
def total_n_queens(n):
    cols = set()
    diagonals = set()
    anti_diagonals = set()
    count = 0

    def backtrack(row):
        nonlocal count
        if row == n:
            count += 1
            return
        for col in range(n):
            diag = row - col
            anti_diag = row + col
            if col in cols or diag in diagonals or anti_diag in anti_diagonals:
                continue
            cols.add(col)
            diagonals.add(diag)
            anti_diagonals.add(anti_diag)
            backtrack(row + 1)
            cols.remove(col)
            diagonals.remove(diag)
            anti_diagonals.remove(anti_diag)

    backtrack(0)
    return count
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) for the recursion stack and tracking sets
